title: Internal Hom and scalar localization under sequential continuity
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and assume that filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the relative derived tensor product [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], and ambient derived internal Hom $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $s$ be a global section of $R$ and put $S=R[1/s]$, the sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], whose underlying $R$-module is the telescope $\varinjlim(R\xrightarrow{s}R\xrightarrow{s}\cdots)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization]. Let $K\in D(R)$ have the following property: for every sequential diagram $(M_n^\bullet)$ of complexes of $R$-module sheaves with one common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced comparison
$$\varinjlim_n H_R(K,M_n^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_R(K,\varinjlim_n M_n^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism; filtered colimits here are exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial complex representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then for every $L\in D(R)$ whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently negative degrees the canonical evaluation-transpose map
$$S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\longrightarrow H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$, natural in $K,L$. Its restriction to $D(R)$, under the evaluation-normalized scalar adjunction, is the sequential-continuity isomorphism $S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\simeq H_R(K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$. No constructibility, completeness, or perfectness hypothesis is imposed beyond the displayed continuity assumption.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary unit-normalized natural isomorphism between tensor localization P₀ and restricted ordinary extension from the localized ring/module comparison, tensor symmetry, and restriction of sheafification. Tensor localization is already exact by LocalizationInverseImageCoherence. Ordinary restriction is fully faithful by the same node, so it reflects finite limits and colimits. Transport preservation across the natural isomorphism and reflect it through restriction to prove exactness of the recorded extension. Localize the termwise ordinary adjunction through Q and identify its left adjoint with the recorded derived extension by uniqueness of left adjoints. The explicit localization unit formula and unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app normalize this identification at each complex.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); localization exactness from sites-modules.tex Tag 03ET (lemma-flatness-sheafification)

proof.text: Ordinary restriction along the localization is fully faithful by LocalizationInverseImageCoherence. Since its left adjoint is exact, restriction preserves K-injective complexes. The existing right-derived full-faithfulness theorem and its comparison with the exact derived functor give fullness of derived restriction. If U is full and F is left adjoint to U, precomposition with the unit X → UFX is injective on maps UFX → UY: lift both maps through fullness and apply injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence. This suffices for the uniqueness assertion after the scalar-Hom isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), normalization; elementary localization multiplication and the two adjunction triangle identities

proof.text: Use the independent-universe scalar module cocone and its colimit proof in LocalizationInverseImageCoherence. Its target is tensor localization P₀, its zeroth leg is the scalar unit, and multiplication by s on its target is invertible. The cocone uniqueness at the zeroth leg proves naturality of every fraction leg. Assemble these cocones degreewise and use evaluation to prove the complex cocone is a colimit, for every complex, including unbounded Hom complexes. Identify P₀(N) with U₀E(N) using the normalized comparison between the localized ring and the localized module, tensor symmetry, and compatibility of restriction with sheafification. Check this identification on the scalar unit, then extend it naturally to complexes and pass to the derived categories using step 2.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits) and Section 03EK; complex-colimit telescope and its normalized legs

proof.text: For the functorial K-injective resolution I with augmentation i, naturality and invertibility of Q(i) give Q(I(s)) = Q(s_I). The natural ordinary-to-derived internal Hom comparison is invertible at K-injective targets; its naturality therefore gives equality after Q between Hom(L,I(s)) and multiplication by s on the Hom complex. Thus the two sequential Hom diagrams are naturally isomorphic after Q. Apply complex_colimit_homotopyColimit to both diagrams. The universal properties of the coproducts give an isomorphism of their first two telescope objects intertwining 1 minus shift. Complete this to a morphism of distinguished triangles; its third component is an isomorphism and preserves every cocone leg. Compose with the displayed continuity comparison for the bounded-below input tower. The resolution comparison and the unit-normalized identifications of step 4 produce an isomorphism β: UF H(K,Q(P)) ≅ H(K,UF Q(P)) satisfying η_H ≫ β = H(K,η_Q(P)).

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), pp. 61–62; agent conditional specialization, using the stated internal-sheaf continuity hypothesis rather than global Hom continuity

proof.text: Let $\chi:FH_R(K,L)\to H_S(FK,FL)$ be the canonical evaluation-transpose map in the statement, and let $\alpha:UH_S(FK,FL)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(K,UFL)$ be the cited evaluation-normalized scalar-Hom isomorphism. Their normalization gives $(\alpha\circ U\chi)\circ\eta_{H_R(K,L)}=H_R(K,\eta_L)$: transposing either side gives evaluation $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\to L$ followed by $\eta_L$, since $\chi$ is the transpose of extended evaluation and $\alpha$ uses the scalar unit on $K$. The target is isomorphic via $\alpha$ to $UN$ for $N=H_S(FK,FL)$. The uniqueness proved in step 3 therefore gives $\alpha\circ U\chi=\beta$. This establishes equality of the actual derived maps, not just their values on the individual telescope legs.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); agent application of evaluation normalization and scalar-unit uniqueness

proof.text: The scalar-Hom adjunction reflects invertibility of the canonical comparison, so steps 5 and 6 prove it for Q(P). Naturality of extended evaluation and transposition gives the comparison square in both variables. Apply it to the isomorphism L ≅ Q(P) to transport invertibility to L. Restriction and the scalar-Hom isomorphism then give invertibility of the restricted comparison; the unit equation and uniqueness follow from step 6 and step 3. The same naturality square gives the final assertion.
